newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage-backed selling boosts US corporate bonds.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage-backed selling boosts US corporate bonds.

text.p: As U.S. interst rates have fallen, investors have begun swapping out of mortgage-backed securities and buying longer-duration corporate bonds in order to extend the duration of their portfolios, several traders said late on Friday.
Traders reported corporates with greater than eight-year maturities have tightened several basis points as as result of an increasing number of these trades.
"People have been short their indexes and are now looking to get longer. We've seen a lot of activity in corporates and it's certainly being driven by mortgage selling."
The market closed early on Friday and will be closed all day on Monday in observance of the Veteran's Day holiday.
Earlier on Friday, spreads on Long Island Lighting Co bonds tightened by 20 basis points on Friday, after a state court awarded the utility as much as $1.16 billion in tax-refunds.

Spreads on Tele-Communications Inc 6 7/8 percent notes of 2006 tightened to 225 basis points over Treasuries from 235 basis points over, after Standard & Poor's held a conference call with investors about the the company's debt rating.
The rating agency current has TCI debt on watch with negative implications.

Robert Nelson, media analyst and director at S&P, told Reuters, "Before making a detemination (about TCI's ratings), we will wait to see whether the company will develop a credible plan to lower debt leverage to well within our guidelines."

He added, "I don't think (TCI's) base business is in trouble. The problem is to take advanteage of opportunties, the company may allow its leverage to be outside of our range for an investment grade credit ratings."

In the high-yield market, Cablevision Systems debt, which had dropped two to three points on Thursday, made up most of the losses in Friday's trading as investors dove in to buy the paper at cheaper levels.
